headline: REA Turns Reverse Engineering Into an Agent Workflow
lede: REA gives coding agents a local command center for dissecting binaries, applications, firmware, and packages. Its evidence-backed reports expose recovered relationships, limitations, and unknowns instead of hiding analysis behind a black box.

headline: VoiceStudio Keeps Voice Production on Your Machine
lede: VoiceStudio brings cloning, dubbing, audiobook production, and audio cleanup into a local-first desktop workflow. With hundreds of languages and interchangeable speech engines, creators can keep models, recordings, and project data away from cloud services.

headline: Context Mode Compresses the Agent’s Working Memory
lede: Context Mode routes bulky tool output through sandboxed execution, returning findings instead of flooding an agent’s context window. SQLite, FTS5, and BM25 retrieval preserve the decisions and evidence that matter across long-running coding sessions.

headline: nvm Makes Node Versions a Shell-Level Choice
lede: nvm keeps Node installations under the developer’s control, switching runtimes with a few dependable shell commands. Project files, aliases, offline installs, and CI guidance make version selection repeatable without touching system packages.

headline: Scientific Skills Catalogs the AI Scientist’s Toolkit
lede: This library packages 163 validated skills across bioinformatics, drug discovery, physics, geospatial analysis, and more. Its standardized interfaces connect agents to over 100 scientific databases while keeping workflows documented, portable, and usable with local models or BYOK deployments.

headline: CLI-Anything Gives Desktop Software an Agent Interface
lede: CLI-Anything builds command-line harnesses that let agents operate tools such as Blender, Kdenlive, Obsidian, and Zotero through predictable workflows. A shared hub, tested skills, input sanitization, and hardened token handling turn scattered integrations into an extensible operating plan.

headline: iFixAi Tests Whether Agents Actually Do Their Jobs
lede: iFixAi red-teams agents against business objectives, organizational requirements, and measurable task outcomes—not just latency or token counts. Scriptable inspections, independent judging, and audit-ready reports give teams a sharper way to expose operational failure.

headline: PentAGI Builds a Self-Hosted Penetration Testing Stack
lede: PentAGI coordinates specialized agents and established security tools inside sandboxed Docker services. Vector memory, optional knowledge graphs, observability dashboards, and broad model support give security teams a traceable platform for planning assessments and producing reports.

headline: Rust Compiles Safety Into Systems Software
lede: Rust combines ownership, borrowing, and lifetime analysis with the raw performance expected from systems programming. Its compiler, standard library, Cargo, Clippy, and diagnostics form a disciplined toolchain for building fast software without routine memory and concurrency failures.

headline: xtool Brings iOS Builds Beyond the Mac
lede: xtool reconstructs core Xcode workflows around Swift Package Manager and a Darwin Swift SDK. Its command line handles project creation, signing, device deployment, and Apple service authentication from Linux, Windows/WSL, or macOS.
